purpose: Primidone is used to help control and prevent seizures in people with epilepsy. It may also be used to treat essential tremor, which is uncontrollable shaking of the hands or other body parts. Your doctor may prescribe it alone or along with other seizure medications.
how_it_works: Primidone works by calming down overactive electrical signals in your brain that can trigger seizures. Your body actually breaks it down into two other active substances — phenobarbital and PEMA — which also help control brain activity. Think of it like a team effort to keep your brain's electrical activity steady and balanced.
common_side_effects: You may feel drowsy, dizzy, or unsteady on your feet, especially when you first start taking it. Some people feel nauseated, have a loss of appetite, or feel unusually tired. Double vision or feeling clumsy are also fairly common at the start of treatment and often improve over time.
warnings: Do not suddenly stop taking primidone without talking to your doctor first, as this can trigger serious or life-threatening seizures. It can cause serious mood changes, depression, or even suicidal thoughts — contact your doctor right away if you notice these. This medication can be habit-forming, and it may affect your ability to drive or operate machinery safely. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may harm the baby.
typical_dosing: Adults usually start with a low dose of 100–125 mg taken at bedtime, and the dose is gradually increased over several weeks to a typical maintenance dose of 750–1500 mg per day, divided into 3 or 4 doses. Children under 8 years old use lower doses. Always take it exactly as prescribed and try to take it at the same times each day.
